Explanation and the formula you should use in Excel so the INDEX-MATCH returns the correct row (not always the first matching region):

Problem
- Your original MATCH(INPUTS!A14,Sheet2!A3:A20,0) finds the first occurrence of the region (e.g. "Regional") and so every row that also uses that MATCH will return values from the first expense row for that region (Advertising & Marketing). You need to identify the row where BOTH the region and the expense name match.

Solution
- Use a MATCH that tests both the region and the expense name together (an INDEX row_num found by MATCH(1, (region_range=region)*(expense_range=expense),0)). Then use a second MATCH to find the correct column (header match).

Formula (put this in C15 and copy across; when copying down it will pick up the expense name from column A of the same row):
=IFNA(
  INDEX(Sheet2!$C$3:$G$20,
        MATCH(1, (Sheet2!$A$3:$A$20=$A$14)*(Sheet2!$B$3:$B$20=$A15), 0),
        MATCH(C$3, Sheet2!$C$1:$G$1, 0)
  ),
0)

Notes:
- Enter as an array formula in older Excel (Ctrl+Shift+Enter). In Excel 365 or newer this works as a normal formula.
- $A$14 is the region dropdown cell. $A15 is the expense name in the same row — using $A15 (column absolute) allows copying across; when you copy down it will change to $A16, etc.
- The first MATCH returns the row where both Sheet2 column A = region and Sheet2 column B = expense. The second MATCH finds the right year/column index from headers (Sheet2!C1:G1) based on the header number in row 3 of INPUTS (C3, D3, ...).
